ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0075 forbids attributing to Volume III a named recurring apparatus or opening disclaimer it does not contain, which touches every Part I section that cites the predecessor. CTD-0036 requires the direct-trust threshold, the governance unit, and the full Scale population to be kept as separate concepts with their evidence and uncertainty stated. CTD-0076 fixes Scale as the singular. CTD-0047 records that Volume III's construction promise is only partly discharged here. CTD-0089 is the parent production item.

findings.summary: The commitment lost its three denials and the standard they set.

evidence.baseline: A specific, concrete, architecturally coherent account of what it would actually take to build the first genuine embodiment of the Providence architecture. Not a vision document. Not a manifesto. Not a set of aspirational principles. A construction plan, as precise as the current state of the inquiry permits.
evidence.shipped: This volume can offer requirements, proposed mechanisms, precedents, failure modes, and explicit questions.

findings.authorizedBy: Catalog 4.3 applied to the three denials, and compression.
findings.diagnosis: 4.3's retention limb requires the rejected alternatives to be plausible. Vision document, manifesto, and aspirational principles are exactly what a reader of a book like this expects, which is why the denials do work rather than clearing rhetorical ground. The shipped list of offerings is accurate and sets no standard, so the chapter no longer commits to anything the reader could hold it to.

findings.summary: The account of how the series accumulates was deleted, along with the map and terrain close.

evidence.baseline: This is how the series accumulates. Not by repeating prior volumes but by building on them precisely enough that the reader experiences genuine intellectual progression, the specific deepening that comes from taking a well-built map into actual terrain and discovering both where the map was accurate and where the terrain has features the map could not show. / The terrain will always have such features. That is not a failure of the map. It is the nature of building.
evidence.shipped: Its value lies in making those obligations harder to hide.

findings.diagnosis: The three sentence close is the chapter's landing and the volume's answer to the reader who fears the architecture will be defended rather than tested. The card names the shift from map to construction among the read-aloud qualities and this is its most complete statement. The shipped landing, harder to hide, is a good sentence and is kept; it does different work.

debtImpact.note: The shipped inventory of what remains unresolved is kept inside the restored commitment, so the chapter promises a plan and states in the same paragraph what prevents it from being complete.
The restored commitment is bounded by the shipped statement of what is unresolved.

reasoning.note: R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Seven em dashes. Two introduced specifications and became colons. Three were parenthetical and became comma pairs. Two separated two movements and became periods, at the accumulation sentence and at the terrain close.

The shipped statement that a completed construction plan cannot be offered while ownership, legal review, technical controls, implementation status, and community evidence remain unresolved, which CTD-0072 requires and the baseline does not say.
The three denials, the construction plan standard, the citation commitment, the accumulation paragraph, and the map and terrain close.

openQuestions: The restored commitment says the reader will have a specific, concrete, architecturally coherent account by the end of the volume. Held beside the shipped statement that a completed plan cannot be offered, the two sit in tension. Both are restored under tonight's policy. Reconciling them is a claim-scope decision that belongs with CTD-0047.

The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required. The section carries the volume's largest single passage of restored commitment language and the clearest case where a restoration and a ledger paydown say different things in neighbouring sentences. Recording the tension rather than resolving it is what the policy required.

audits.auditor: editorial-agent, generation 1 of the twenty-rule re-render lane
audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: the CTD-0072 bounding is two sentences appended to the commitment paragraph and names exactly the unresolved obligations the item tracks; it does not soften the restored three denials before it, which is the correction applied at width. The tension between the restored commitment and the bounding is already an open question tied to CTD-0047 and stands. R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the commitment keeps its committing half in full, which matters because this is the section a compression pass would most naturally hedge; the three denials and the construction-plan standard both survive. R-PAIRED-DELETION: pattern language, iron law of megaprojects, stabilitas, and the translation problem were swept; each term is self-contained here and none dangles. Citations were re-verified intact through the punctuation repairs: Alexander 1979 and 1977 with both co-authors, Flyvbjerg, Eisenhardt, Katz and Gartner, Aldrich, and the quoted iron law kept in its original single quotes. R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT: the kept boundings bound under CTD-0072, no credit owed, stated explicitly. R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK, R-REFRAIN-COST, R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Thirty-six of forty-nine baseline sentences survive verbatim, the highest absolute survival in Part I, and the remainder is fully attributed to punctuation repairs and the two documented CTD-0072 sentences. No prose change required.
corrections: The original record's punctuation inventory of seven marks covers the chapter body; the research lineage and open questions passages carry a further seven of the same two forms, parenthetical pairs become comma pairs and one period at the operational-mistakes sentence, all verified against the diff. One further divergence attributed: the baseline's in its human architecture chapters stands as in its human architecture, dropping a structural attribution to Volume III consistent with CTD-0075's caution.
